## SECTION 1 – SERIOUS CRIME PREVENTION ORDERS

## Claim form – application for a SCPO

## 1.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.1] An application for a SCPO must be started by way of a Part 8 claim form, although the court may decide during the proceedings that it would be more appropriate to continue the proceedings in accordance with Part 7.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.1] (Rule 8.1(3) allows the court to make an order that the claim continue as if the claimant had not used the Part 8 procedure.)

## 1.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] The claim form must –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] (1) identify which provisions of section 2(1) of the 2007 Act the applicant relies on and under each provision identified, set out the details of the allegations that the respondent has been involved in serious crime (whether in England and Wales or elsewhere);

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] (2) set out the applicant’s grounds for contending that the proposed terms of the SCPO are appropriate for the purpose of protecting the public in accordance with section 1(3) of the 2007 Act; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] (3) include details of any third party whom the applicant believes is likely to be significantly adversely affected by the SCPO and the nature of that adverse effect.

## 1.3

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.3] The claim form must be accompanied by a draft of the SCPO for which the application is made. The terms of the draft SCPO must include any proposed dates, including those upon which the applicant proposes that the SCPO should come into force and cease to be in force.

## 1.4

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.4] Where it is alleged that the respondent has committed a serious offence, the claim form must be accompanied by evidence that the respondent has been convicted of the offence. Where a certificate of conviction can be obtained, this must be put in evidence.

## 1.5

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] Where it is alleged that the respondent has been convicted of an offence in another jurisdiction, the applicant must put in evidence –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (a) a document from the appropriate public authority in the jurisdiction concerned certifying that the respondent has after due process of law been convicted of the offence; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (b) where the document is not in English, a translation of that document into English –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (i) certified by a notary public or other qualified person; or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (ii) accompanied by written evidence confirming that the translation is accurate.

## Applications by third parties to make representations

## 2.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 2.1] The evidence in support of an application made under section 9 of the 2007 Act must contain details of why the third party believes the proposed order would be likely to have a significant adverse effect on that third party.

## Application to vary or discharge a SCPO

## 3.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] The application notice or claim form must contain –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (1) where the applicant is the person who is the subject of the SCPO, details of the change of circumstances affecting the SCPO;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (2) where the applicant seeks to vary the SCPO, any grounds advanced by the applicant for contending that the terms of the SCPO as varied would protect the public in accordance with section 17(1) of the 2007 Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (2A) where the applicant for the SCPO seeks to vary the SCPO –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (a) details of any third party whom the applicant believes is likely to be significantly adversely affected by the proposed variation to the SCPO; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (b) details of the nature of that adverse effect;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (3) where the applicant seeks to vary the SCPO and is a third party or the person who is the subject of the SCPO –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (a) particulars of why the applicant believes the applicant is significantly adversely affected by the SCPO;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (b) particulars of how condition A or B in section 17 of the 2007 Act is met; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (c) particulars relied upon to establish that the purpose of the application is not to make the SCPO more onerous on the person who is the subject of the order; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (4) where the application is for the discharge of the SCPO and the applicant is a third party or the person who is the subject of the SCPO, particulars of –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (a) why the applicant believes the applicant is significantly adversely affected by the SCPO; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (b) how condition A or B in section 18 of the 2007 Act is met.

## 3.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.2] Where the application is to vary or discharge a SCPO made by the Crown Court, the claim form must be accompanied by a copy of the SCPO made by the Crown Court.

## Where to make an application

## 4.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 4.1] An application for an SCPO or relating to an SCPO must be filed in the Administrative Court at the Royal Courts of Justice.

## SECTION 3 – REFERRAL OF RELEASE DECISIONS

## Where to make an application

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > Where to make an application] 5.1 Any application concerning the referral of a release decision must be filed in the Administrative Court at the Royal Courts of Justice.

## Victim personal statements

## 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] by the maker of the VPS or another person;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] in whole or in part or in a summary; or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] in person or through a video link or recording or by some other means,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] having had regard to—

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] the wishes of the maker of the VPS;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] the contents of the VPS; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] the potential for any harm to the victim or any other person which may arise from the VPS being read in court.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] (2) Where a VPS is read in court under paragraph (1), neither the maker nor the reader shall be cross-examined on it.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] (3) Practice Direction 1A applies to any person referred to in this paragraph.

## Licence conditions

## 7.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 7.1] If the court makes an order requiring the applicant to give effect to the Parole Board’s direction to release the prisoner on licence, before deciding whether to include directions as to the conditions to be included in the respondent’s licence on release, the court shall have regard to the guidance in the Ministry of Justice’s and His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service’s Licence Conditions Policy Framework: Licence conditions policy framework – GOV.UK (opens in a new tab) .
